H1.text: Here is a strange set. All the even prime numbers bigger than two.

H2.text: Four? Two times two, so not prime. Six? Two times three. Eight? Two times four. Every even number after two splits by two.

H3.text: Aarav checked a long list at his study table and found none at all.

H4.text: So is this set nothing? Or is it something?

H5.text: It is something. A set with nothing inside. And it opens a whole family: empty, finite, infinite and universal sets.

E2.text: A set that has no element at all is called the empty set. It is also called the null set, or the void set.

E3.text: We write it with this symbol, phi. Or as two curly brackets with nothing between them.

E4.text: Watch the test run on even primes bigger than two. Four is out. Six, out. Eight, ten, twelve, all out.

E5.text: The bag stays empty, and the count stays at zero. The number of elements in phi is zero.

E6.text: More empty sets: the natural numbers between one and two. The odd numbers whose square is four. Every test, and nothing passes.

K1.text: Side by side. The empty set is an empty box. Nothing inside.

K2.text: The set containing zero is a box with one thing inside: the number zero. Zero is something, so this set is not empty.

K3.text: Now you try. The set containing phi. Phi inside curly brackets. Is it empty? Pause and decide.

K4.text: Not empty! It is a box holding one thing, an empty box. So it has exactly one element.

G2.text: A set is finite if it is empty, or if you can count its elements and the counting comes to an end.

G3.text: The days of the week. Seven elements, so finite. The letters of SCHOOL. Five elements, finite.

G4.text: We write n of S for the number of different elements in S.

G5.text: Now watch the natural numbers. One, two, three. Keep counting.

G6.text: A thousand. A million. A billion. The counter never reaches an end.

G7.text: A set that is not finite is called infinite. The natural numbers, the integers, and all the points on a line are infinite.

G8.text: In roster form we show the pattern and add three dots. But the real numbers have no pattern to list, so they need set builder form.

G9.text: Quick one. The natural numbers less than one crore. Finite, or infinite? Pause and think.

GA.text: Finite! The set is huge, but the counting stops just before one crore. Big is not the same as endless.

U2.text: In any problem, all the sets we talk about come from one big basic set. That basic set is the universal set, written U.

U3.text: If our sets are the students who ride a bicycle and the students who walk, the universal set is all the students in the class.

U4.text: We draw U as a rectangle, and every other set sits inside it.

U5.text: U depends on the problem. For sets of integers, U could be the rational numbers, or the real numbers.

T1.text: Remember this. Empty means nothing inside. Finite means the counting ends. Infinite means it never does.

W2.text: Which of these sets are empty, which are finite, and which are infinite? All four use natural numbers.

W3.text: One. Two x minus one equals zero gives x equals one half. That is not a natural number, so this set is empty.

W4.text: Two. x minus one, times x minus two, equals zero. So x is one or two. Finite, with two elements.

W5.text: Three. The factors of twelve are one, two, three, four, six and twelve. Finite, with six elements.

W6.text: Four. The prime numbers never run out, so this set is infinite.

X2.text: Many students write that the set containing zero is the empty set.

X3.text: But zero is an element. The set containing zero has one element. Only the empty set has none. The same goes for the set containing phi.

J1.text: Where is this asked? Expect questions like: which of these sets are empty, and which are finite or infinite?

Q1.text: Exam level now. How many of these five sets are empty? Pause and solve.

A2.text: A. No real number squared gives minus one. Empty.

A3.text: B. x squared minus three x plus two is x minus one, times x minus two. So B is one and two. Not empty.

A4.text: C. No integer lies strictly between one and two. Empty. D. The square root of two is not rational. Empty.

A5.text: E holds one element, the empty set itself. Not empty. So three sets are empty: A, C and D.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. Give two examples of the empty set.

Y3.text: Two. Is the set of all points on a line finite or infinite?

Y4.text: Three. Why is the set containing zero not empty?
